question: After a user-coordinated orderly host reboot, does the unchanged default-environment primitive transfer test complete?
hypothesis: A012 reproduced the first host-to-device copy timeout with and without SDMA, outside all project model/checkpoint logic. A fresh boot may clear persistent runtime/device state; a successful postboot test would support a state-dependent failure without identifying the original cause.

sources.consequence: Retain explicit stage logging and synchronization; require the whole copy/arithmetic round trip, not allocation alone.
SDMA disabling did not restore copying. Return to unchanged default settings after reboot; no extra environment-variable sweep or production workaround is authorized by this diagnostic.
Propose an orderly user-coordinated reboot; never force it, bypass inhibitors, or schedule it without authorization. Host shutdown affects desktop applications as well as compute.
Record the current boot UUID and refuse the postboot probe until it changes. Elapsed time or a missing PID is not evidence of a reboot.

sources.sections: process, list and reset command help
sources.consequence: Map GPU0 to BDF0000:03:00.0 and inspect actual DRM clients/connectors. It drives two connected displays; do not issue a live device reset or driver reload.

sources.sections: Popen wait, timeouts, terminate/kill and environment
sources.consequence: Reuse the externally supervised primitive with45-second work deadline and bounded10/5-second cleanup. Close shared budget only after child exit.

differences: This record adds only a host-state intervention proposal and one postboot diagnostic. Reboot execution requires user coordination because it interrupts a live workstation. The existing approval for six serial checkpoint continuations persists. No training recipe, package, driver, model or data change is proposed.
contrary_evidence: Reboot may not repair a persistent software/configuration/hardware issue. A passing tiny probe cannot establish full-training stability. The related R9700 issue9279 uses different hardware/runtime/workload and does not diagnose this machine.

protocol.preparation: Preserve current boot ID, A012 records/logs/reviews, GPU/DRM/kernel observations and six recovery checkpoint/config/metric hashes. Verify exact original7dfc837 source and all expected checkpoint hashes. No trainers or diagnostic children remain. Record a concrete handoff before asking for user action.
protocol.host_action: User performs an orderly reboot after saving desktop work, or explicitly authorizes an agent action separately. This record is not reboot authorization. Do not reset a live display GPU, stop display services, force shutdown, install packages or alter driver/runtime settings.
protocol.postboot: Require changed boot_id, unchanged six checkpoint/config/metric hashes and original source. Run exactly the A012 baseline probe bytes once, original interpreter/env, dedicated GPU0, same4096float32 allocation/H2D/synchronize/add/synchronize/D2H/equality sequence, external45+10+5second cap. Refuse before boot change, active compute process, changed source/artifact, exhausted ledger or memory ceiling. Preserve exact script and predecessor review hashes.
protocol.review: Literature-review the postboot result before any continuation. On success prepare a distinct attempt directory for the first unchanged original continuation; preserve failed A010 attempt and require observable new progress. On failure stop retries and prepare a runtime issue reproducer. No automatic review or training launch.
protocol.verification: CPU-only syntax and same-boot refusal checks before handoff; validate research/review digests and repository custody. The refusal check must create no GPU context, result directory or budget interval.

success: Postboot primitive exits0 with exact full round trip inside deadline. Preparation success refers only to verified preserved artifacts and guarded handoff.
stop: No host action without user coordination. One postboot primitive maximum; no same-boot retry or SDMA variation. Stop on changed evidence, process conflict or test failure, preserving technical_blocked rather than treating it as a model negative.

resources.training_device: none; one dedicated GPU primitive only after boot change
